description: We are TukCoders, a team of passionate software engineering students participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Peshawar, Pakistan. Our team focuses on web development, creativity, and innovative problem-solving. We aim to build an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that makes space exploration fun, educational, and accessible. Together, we code, innovate, and explore beyond limits!
summary: Lunar Base Rescue is an interactive 3D educational game developed by Team TUKCODERS for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Players explore a lunar outpost and make important engineering decisions involving electricity, water recycling, radiation protection, and astronaut safety. Built using Godot and GDScript, the game uses historical NASA space weather data and lunar lighting references to help young learners understand real space exploration challenges through interactive gameplay.
details:
Problem

Space missions require astronauts to balance limited resources, including electricity, water, life support, and radiation protection. These engineering trade-offs can be difficult for young students to understand through traditional learning.

Our Solution

Lunar Base Rescue is an interactive 3D educational simulation that allows students to explore a lunar outpost, interact with mission stations, and make decisions affecting astronaut safety and resource availability.

How It Works

Players control an astronaut and visit three mission stations:

  1. Power Control: Balance solar energy and electricity requirements.
  2. Radiation Shelter: Respond to a solar particle event and protect astronauts.
  3. Water Systems: Make decisions about water recycling and battery usage.

Each decision introduces an engineering trade-off and helps students understand its consequences.

NASA Data Integration

The project includes historical Solar Energetic Particle (SEP) records from NASA's DONKI database and lunar lighting references from NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio.

The NASA observations provide scientific context. Battery points and other gameplay effects are simplified educational simulation values, not actual NASA measurements.

Technologies Used

  • Godot 4.6
  • GDScript
  • 3D game development
  • JSON data integration
  • NASA DONKI
  • NASA Scientific Visualization Studio

Educational Impact

The game encourages students to develop problem-solving skills, critical thinking, resource management, and an understanding of engineering decisions involved in lunar exploration.

Developed by Team TUKCODERS for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
